paper_core_claims.claim: NoviCode defines natural-language programming as generation of executable programs with non-trivial sequences, conditions, loops, and API calls from novice descriptions plus an API specification.
The benchmark evaluates generated programs by executing human-authored unit-test suites against a simulated API/data model rather than by string form alone.
The proposed pipeline maps natural language x to a linearized compact AST z and then deterministically parses and expands z to a Python AST and surface program y.
Across most tested models, the cAST representation improves functional pass rates over direct text-to-code, but not uniformly for every model and metric.
Even the best reported setup remains weak on implicit loops and exhibits substantial runtime and semantic errors.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A generated Python program is the executable function-like artifact; the paper treats the novice utterance and independent API specification as its high-level specification, and cAST as a control-flow-focused intermediate representation.

representation_or_carrier.intermediate_carrier: linearized compact abstract syntax tree retaining sequences, conditions, and loops while leaving basic operations as code-form leaves
representation_or_carrier.artifact_carrier: Python AST and executable Python source

specification_language: A paired specification consisting of everyday natural language plus typed Python API classes, entity interfaces, action methods, and text/entity resolution operations; it is not a formal contract calculus.

compiler_or_generator.learned_stage: An LLM or fine-tuned encoder-decoder model generates either Python directly or the linearized cAST from the utterance and API context.
compiler_or_generator.deterministic_stage: The supplied parser reconstructs cAST, expands it to a Python AST, and uses Python's ast package to emit executable code.
compiler_or_generator.boundary: Only the z-to-y stage is described as deterministic; the x-to-z model remains probabilistic and error-prone.

interpreter_or_runtime: Python execution with a mock API implementation and mutable data model seeded by each test scenario; generated code is embedded and executed before assertions inspect resulting state.
composition_rule: Hierarchical tree composition of sequences, conditions, and loops, with assignments and API calls represented as leaf code. This supports nested control flow but does not define general multi-artifact routing or conflict resolution.
state_or_effect_model: API actions read or mutate a simulated domain data model. Tests seed entities, execute generated code, and assert state changes. The paper does not supply a typed algebra of effects, permissions, rollback, or transaction semantics.
uncertainty_model: Model uncertainty is operationalized only through stochastic sample generation and pass@k. The paper does not define calibrated probabilities, fuzzy semantics, epistemic confidence, or uncertainty propagation through the compiled program.

validation_regime.primary: 150 human-crafted execution-based test problems with multiple scenarios and assertions over the mock data model
validation_regime.granularity: finite behavioral observations for the tested scenarios, including state effects and some control-flow cases
validation_regime.known_risk: Finite tests can miss behaviors; the paper itself notes cost-limited coverage and discusses false-positive and true-negative risks of functional tests.

equivalence_notions.boundary: Passing tests is observational agreement on sampled scenarios, not full program equivalence.
Assertions inspect affected data-model state, but only within the mock API and finite suite.
The evaluation intentionally permits different code forms.
No proof, bisimulation, refinement relation, or exhaustive semantics is supplied.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper identifies the arXiv version, dataset/code repository, crowd-source and synthetic-data construction processes, API/test creation, model setups, and experimental configurations. It does not provide a versioned registry for generated programs, artifact lineage across compilation, deployment monitoring, drift detection, supersession, or retirement.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Only 150 of 1,200 collected utterances received human-crafted test suites because test creation is expensive and requires Python/API expertise.
Fine-tuning relies on 40K synthesized examples; the paper states that performance depends on a sufficiently large synthetic training set.
The API runtime is simulated, so success does not establish safe or reliable behavior against real email, calendar, weather, or other external services.
The cAST approach does not improve every model/metric combination; GPT-3.5 pass@1 and DeepSeek-Coder results include regressions relative to direct code.
Loops expressed implicitly are recovered poorly: the reported control-flow success is 16% for loops versus 68% for sequences and 46% for conditions.
Error analysis reports malformed cAST, runtime exceptions, and executable-but-semantically-wrong programs; finite tests do not eliminate these risks.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that cAST and generated Python are formally semantically equivalent for all programs.
It does not validate a general Function OS architecture or the point project as a whole.
It does not provide a first-class execution-trace object, general router, versioned registry, rollback protocol, permissions model, or artifact lifecycle governance.
It does not establish real-world safety or empirical reliability against production APIs beyond the benchmark's mock data model.
It does not support treating model sampling success or finite test passing as mathematical proof, causal identification, or exhaustive behavioral equivalence.

GAP-015.reason: Direct evidence for separating novice/API specification, cAST intermediate representation, Python AST, and executable source as distinct carriers; no universal carrier taxonomy.

GAP-016.reason: Direct, source-specific evidence for a learned generator followed by deterministic cAST parsing and Python AST/source emission, with runtime execution kept distinct.

GAP-017.reason: API signatures and state-changing actions give a practical contract/effect surface, but no formal effect system, pre/postcondition language, permissions, or rollback semantics.

GAP-018.reason: cAST explicitly composes sequences, conditions, and loops, but the paper does not address routing among independently versioned functions or artifacts.

GAP-019.reason: Execution-based test suites provide a concrete limited behavioral-acceptance regime and demonstrate why form equality is too strong; the confirmation is limited to finite benchmark observations.

GAP-020.reason: pass@k and dataset provenance do not constitute a lifecycle/provenance schema or probabilistic/fuzzy program semantics.

N1_FunctionSpec.reason: Everyday-language intent plus API specification is a concrete but non-formal function specification.

N2_Representation.reason: The source explicitly distinguishes utterance, cAST, Python AST, and source program representations.

N3_Compiler.reason: The x-to-z learned generation and deterministic z-to-y compilation stages are described and implemented separately.

N4_Artifact.reason: cAST and emitted Python are concrete artifacts, but artifact identity, signing, packaging, and version policy are absent.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Python plus the mock API/data model executes generated programs, but this is a benchmark runtime rather than a general interpreter contract.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Tests observe outcomes and exceptions; the paper does not define or persist a first-class execution trace.

N7_Validator.reason: Human-crafted test suites, state assertions, pass@k, and error analysis form a concrete finite validator regime.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Tree composition covers nested control flow but not runtime routing, selection, fallback, or multi-artifact conflict resolution.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: No registry state machine, version identity, supersession, drift, or retirement mechanism is defined.

source_specific_reasoning: NoviCode is unusually relevant to the Compiler, Representation, and Validator parts of the candidate Function OS because it exposes a three-stage boundary: high-level intent plus API specification, a control-flow-focused cAST, and executable Python. The paper also supplies direct negative evidence against collapsing behavioral success into semantic equivalence: tests are finite, the runtime is mocked, loops are recovered poorly, and executable programs often remain semantically wrong. Therefore the source supports a limited staged-compiler and behavioral-acceptance projection, but it cannot support a general Function OS, formal equivalence, production safety, or lifecycle registry claim.
projection_boundary: All GAP and Function OS impacts above are 121CX architectural projections from the paper's bounded claims. They are not claims made by the authors and are not mathematical proof, causal identification, empirical validation of the point architecture, or final truth freeze.

paper_core_claims.claim: A code LLM proposes multiple implementations per function and the synthesizer selects compatible combinations by executing constraints, using topological order for acyclic dependencies and joint search within SCCs for recursive dependencies.

paper_core_claims.claim: On the evaluated competition-level APPS subset, Parsel raises pass rate from the compared 14.5% direct baseline to 25.5%, and an ablation that keeps the high-level plan but emits Python directly drops to 6% on the sampled comparison.
With GPT-4 and generated tests, Parsel reports about 85% HumanEval pass@1 versus the cited 67% state of the art, while generated tests themselves may be wrong and are ranked using CodeT.

The framework's benefits are bounded by code-LLM capability, incomplete or absent constraints, exponential combination growth inside large SCCs, target-language differences, and dependence on mutable closed-model services.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a named natural-language description with optional arguments and return variables, references to callable dependencies, multiple target-language implementations, and constraints used to select acceptable implementations.

representation_or_carrier.specification_carrier: indentation-scoped Parsel text containing descriptions, references, headers, and constraints
representation_or_carrier.dependency_carrier: function call graph and derived test-dependency graph partitioned into strongly connected components
representation_or_carrier.candidate_carrier: sets of code-LLM-generated function implementation strings
representation_or_carrier.artifact_carrier: composed target-language program, including Python, C++, Lean, or VirtualHome-oriented output in the paper's examples

specification_language: Parsel's semi-formal DSL: function-name/argument/optional-return descriptions in natural language, indentation-based scope, explicit references, input-output or language-specific constraints, and optional global headers. Constraint representation and execution are target-language specific.

compiler_or_generator.decomposition_stage: A human or LLM converts a task or high-level plan into Parsel descriptions and dependencies.
compiler_or_generator.implementation_stage: A code LLM samples implementations for each described function using child signatures and descriptions as context.
compiler_or_generator.synthesis_stage: The Parsel compiler parses the program, builds dependency/SCC graphs, tests candidate implementation sets, composes solved SCCs, and emits the target program.
compiler_or_generator.failure_and_extension: Compilation can fail on an SCC, optionally trigger function infilling or repeated decomposition, or exhaust the candidate/constraint search.

interpreter_or_runtime: There is no single Parsel runtime. Candidate constraints and final artifacts are evaluated by target-specific mechanisms: Python assertions/evaluation, compilation and execution for C++, proof checking for Lean, or VirtualHome executability for robotic plans.
composition_rule: For acyclic graphs, implement children before parents in post-order. For recursive or mutually dependent functions, jointly sample implementation tuples within each SCC and accept a set satisfying all applicable constraints. Functions lacking local constraints inherit test dependency from constrained parents or use generated tests at the top level.
state_or_effect_model: Parsel models call and test dependencies but does not define a general typed state/effect calculus. Side effects, exceptions, timeouts, environmental state, and proof obligations are delegated to the chosen target language and constraint evaluator.
uncertainty_model: Uncertainty is operational: sample multiple decompositions and implementations, randomly explore combinations without replacement, measure pass@n times k, and use CodeT scores when tests are generated. This is search under stochastic model outputs, not a calibrated probabilistic or fuzzy program semantics.

validation_regime.local: function-level input-output constraints or target-language-specific checks
validation_regime.composed: constraints on parents or SCCs after candidate functions are linked
validation_regime.boundary: Constraint satisfaction is only as strong as test coverage and correctness; generated tests can be wrong and target-language validators differ.

equivalence_notions.boundary: Candidate implementations are interchangeable only insofar as the available constraints and dependent functions cannot distinguish them.
Passing APPS/HumanEval/VirtualHome evaluations does not establish behavior outside those tasks or tests.
No general semantics-preservation proof relates descriptions, all candidate implementations, and emitted programs.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The source provides an arXiv version, public code repository, prompts, hyperparameters, sample budgets, compiled examples, and target-language configuration details. It also implements prompt-response caching for stability. It does not define durable artifact identities, signed provenance, deployed-version monitoring, drift detection, supersession, or retirement in a versioned registry.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: A function that the underlying code LLM cannot implement remains a failure unless further decomposition makes it simpler.
Candidate combinations grow exponentially with the largest SCC and can also be costly when constraints are sparse.
Generated tests may be wrong; assertions cannot determine all semantic properties, and missing constraints allow incorrect implementations to survive.
Constraint meaning, execution, and prompts vary across target languages, so one validator/compiler contract is not shown to generalize unchanged.

The strongest reported implementation depends on closed Codex/GPT-4 services whose behavior, availability, price, and rate limits can change; the tested 2.7B CodeGen model solved none of 25 sampled APPS problems.
The APPS evaluation does not cover real programs with thousands of lines, which the paper identifies as a missing benchmark.
VirtualHome executability is easier to test than task correctness; correctness relied on a small human-ranking study and did not assert subsequent world-state relations.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that satisfying finite constraints makes an implementation semantically equivalent to its natural-language description.
It does not provide a universal interpreter, typed effect system, permission model, rollback protocol, execution-trace schema, or versioned artifact registry.
It does not establish that combinatorial composition remains tractable for arbitrarily large SCCs or weakly constrained programs.
It does not validate the point architecture as a whole, freeze a Function OS, or turn benchmark improvements into mathematical proof or production reliability.

GAP-016.reason: It gives a concrete staged compiler/synthesizer and explicitly separates target-specific execution or proof checking from compilation.

GAP-018.reason: DAG/SCC decomposition, dependency-aware synthesis, candidate combination, and constraint-based selection directly support bounded composition; runtime routing and fallback policy remain absent.

GAP-019.reason: Constraint execution and benchmark tests are explicit behavioral acceptance mechanisms, with clear evidence that their equivalence reach is finite and test-relative.

GAP-020.reason: Sampling and caching do not amount to lifecycle/provenance governance or probabilistic/fuzzy semantics.

N2_Representation.reason: The Parsel program, dependency/SCC graphs, candidate sets, and target program are distinct representations.

N3_Compiler.reason: The parser, graph builder, code-LLM generator, SCC solver, tester, and composer form a concrete compiler/synthesizer pipeline.

N4_Artifact.reason: Candidate functions and composed programs are artifacts, but durable identity, packaging, signing, and version semantics are absent.

N5_Interpreter.reason: Execution is explicitly delegated to Python/C++/Lean/VirtualHome-specific evaluators; a common interpreter boundary is implied but not specified.

N6_ExecutionTrace.reason: Test outcomes and failures are used internally, but no first-class persistent execution-trace object is defined.

N7_Validator.reason: Constraints, generated tests, target evaluators, benchmark tests, and human plan judgments provide direct bounded validation evidence.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Dependency/SCC ordering and combinatorial candidate selection directly support the Composer portion; this does not confirm a general runtime Router.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Caching improves repeated generation stability but is not a versioned registry or lifecycle state machine.

source_specific_reasoning: Parsel exposes more of the candidate Function OS pipeline than a generic code-generation benchmark: FunctionSpec is a real DSL surface, Representation includes dependency/SCC graphs and candidate sets, Compiler performs LLM generation plus constrained graph synthesis, Composer combines implementations, and Validator executes language-specific constraints. The same paper supplies decisive boundaries: constraints can be absent or wrong, SCC search is exponential, target evaluators differ, and closed-model drift undermines reproducibility. Thus it confirms a bounded architecture projection but not formal equivalence, general routing, lifecycle governance, or a frozen Function OS.

paper_core_claims.claim: COGEX fine-tunes language models to map a task instruction and optional input to a Python-like pseudo-program, a function call, and an output dictionary containing intermediate and final values.
Undefined leaf functions are intentionally allowed, and the same language model emulates rather than actually executes the generated program so that latent knowledge can supply those leaves.
COTACS samples reusable task-level pseudo-programs, filters them by a training threshold, ranks them on a development split, and optionally majority-votes the top programs at test time.

Across the reported nine tasks, 1000-example COTACS outperforms the compared Alpaca or two-shot baselines on 8 of 9 tasks for both evaluated Llama-2 sizes; the ablations show that gains and preferred adaptation method vary by task and data volume.
paper_core_claims.anchors: Sections 3.1-3.3; Tables 1-2; Figures 2, 4, and 5; PDF pages 5-9

paper_core_claims.claim: The authors directly document that the language-model emulator can return results inconsistent with the pseudo-program, can be less appropriate than a real interpreter for precise algorithms, and incurs extra generation overhead.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a Python-shaped reasoning scaffold with a name, arguments, comments or steps, calls that may be undefined, and a returned dictionary of intermediate and final values. Its meaning is completed operationally by a language model's emulation rather than by executable definitions for every call.

representation_or_carrier.task_carrier: natural-language instruction plus optional instance input
representation_or_carrier.program_carrier: Python-like function text and an instantiated function call
representation_or_carrier.reasoning_carrier: inline natural-language plan comments plus undefined semantic leaf-function names
representation_or_carrier.output_carrier: dictionary containing intermediate values and the final answer
representation_or_carrier.adaptation_carrier: one or a top-k set of reusable task-level program strings selected by COTACS

specification_language: The specification is hybrid and weakly formal: a natural-language task instruction, optional input argument, Python surface syntax, comments naming reasoning steps, underspecified leaf-function identifiers, and an expected answer field in an output dictionary. It does not provide types, contracts, effects, or complete executable definitions for the semantic leaves.

compiler_or_generator.training_data_stage: GPT-4 reformats Alpaca outputs and inputs, creates a general-purpose natural-language plan, then instantiates that plan as a Python-like function with intermediate outputs.
compiler_or_generator.model_stage: A LoRA-fine-tuned Llama-2 or Code Llama model generates a pseudo-program, function call, and emulated output from the instruction and input.
compiler_or_generator.search_stage: COTACS samples candidate programs, filters them using a training-performance threshold, ranks them on a development split, and retains one or more task-level program strings.
compiler_or_generator.boundary: This is neural generation and empirical program-string selection, not a deterministic semantics-preserving compiler.

interpreter_or_runtime: The runtime is an LM emulator: it generates the call and predicted output, including values for undefined leaf functions, without executing the text in Python. For precise algorithmic tasks the paper itself says direct interpreter execution may be preferable. The observed inconsistency between code and output means this boundary is intentionally flexible but semantically unreliable.
composition_rule: Sequential data dependencies in the generated pseudo-program and its intermediate-output dictionary provide local composition. COTACS composes only at the ensemble level by retaining top-k whole programs and majority-voting their answers; it does not define general multi-function artifact linking, runtime routing, or conflict semantics.
state_or_effect_model: Intermediate dictionary fields expose selected internal values, and program variables provide transient data flow. There is no typed state model, effect algebra, external-resource policy, permissions model, transactional boundary, rollback, exception contract, or persistent execution-trace schema.
uncertainty_model: Uncertainty is handled through stochastic candidate generation, a user-defined training threshold, development-set ranking, low-temperature answer sampling, and optional majority vote over top-k programs. These are empirical search and ensemble procedures, not calibrated predictive uncertainty or probabilistic/fuzzy program semantics.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The model can produce an output inconsistent with the displayed code, so the pseudo-program is not guaranteed to be a faithful execution trace or explanation.
Undefined leaf functions deliberately move semantics into latent model behavior; their implementation, state effects, and failure modes are neither executable nor formally specified.
For precisely describable algorithmic tasks, actual interpreter execution may be preferable to LM emulation.
Generating intermediate variables adds computational overhead relative to a conventional interpreter.
COTACS selects programs against train/development examples, so its acceptance evidence is task- and split-relative and does not exclude selection overfitting.
The nine-task experiments and 7B/13B models do not establish behavior for arbitrary tasks, larger systems, production workloads, or changing model checkpoints.
Benchmark correctness does not provide a typed effect model, safety policy, rollback mechanism, formal equivalence, or lifecycle governance.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that a pseudo-program denotes the same computation as the language model's returned dictionary.
It does not provide a general semantics for undefined functions, a real universal interpreter, or a semantics-preserving compiler.
It does not establish calibrated uncertainty, formal compositional equivalence, persistent traces, runtime safety, or a versioned registry.
It does not validate the point architecture as a whole, prove a Function OS, or turn benchmark improvements into mathematical proof, causal identification, or production validation.

paper_core_claims.claim: DeepONet represents a nonlinear operator through a branch network over finitely sampled input-function values and a trunk network over output coordinates, combined by an inner product plus optional bias.
Under compact-domain, compact input-family, continuity, and universal-approximator assumptions, the generalized branch/trunk architecture can approximate continuous nonlinear operators uniformly.

The theorem controls representation or approximation capacity, not optimization error, finite-sample generalization, network-size complexity, or learnability; these remain separate and often dominant.

Across 16 curated explicit, implicit, deterministic, and stochastic examples generated primarily from known numerical solvers, the authors report lower generalization error than selected baselines and fast empirical error decay in several regimes.

The paper's stochastic examples propagate random-process inputs or predict pathwise/statistical outputs, but they do not establish a unified calibrated uncertainty interface for unseen production distributions.

Because the training targets are produced by reference solvers, the trained surrogate cannot exceed those solvers' accuracy on that evidence; the paper claims inference speedup after expensive offline training, not autonomous correctness.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is an element of a compact family in C(K), operationalized by values at shared sensor points, orthogonal-polynomial coefficients, an image grid, or a truncated Karhunen-Loève representation. An operator maps an input function u to an output function G(u); the trained artifact evaluates G(u)(y) for a queried output coordinate y.

paper_core_claims.claim: LORAUTER makes representative tasks first-class routing intermediaries: labeled validation queries define task embeddings and a validation-performance map from tasks to adapters.
At inference, a query is embedded, matched to the top-K task representations, and the corresponding compatible LoRA outputs are fused with softmax-normalized similarity weights.

Inference-time selection compares against T representative tasks rather than N adapters, yielding O(T) retrieval under the paper's accounting; task-adapter pairing remains an offline evaluation problem over the adapter pool.
On a reused 48-task LLaMA2 benchmark, weighted fusion reaches 101.2% and 98.8% of task-aligned normalized performance in-domain and 88.4% and 86.8% in OOD settings for 7B and 13B models respectively.
On 1,567 rank-bounded public LLaMA2-7B adapters without the curated pool, the paper reports 89.6% semi-OOD and 85.7% OOD normalized performance, but does not compare all baselines at that scale.
Successive Halving reduces validation evaluations needed to approach peak adapter-selection performance by more than twofold in a 100-run resampling study.

paper_core_claims.claim: L2R trains a separate LoRA adapter for each arriving task while deactivating prior adapters, so the newly trained adapter is isolated from earlier adapter modules.
After task-adapter training, layerwise routers learn from a small labeled replay memory to allocate multiple task adapters independently through Gumbel-sigmoid outputs.
L2R-wavg composes adapter outputs with learned weights, whereas L2R-merge forms a weighted parameter merge; the former costs more inference computation but avoids some merge interference.

Across BERT-base MTL5 and WOS plus AfroXLMR-base AfriSenti task sequences, L2R-wavg is competitive with the compared PEFT continual-learning baselines in CIL and TIL, while not winning every dataset and setup.
Increasing replay-memory size generally improves routing, and replacing Gumbel-sigmoid with softmax especially degrades WOS CIL performance in the reported ablation.

The reported efficiency comparison is theoretical FLOPs for batch size one and sequence length 128; it does not measure end-to-end latency, memory construction, router training, or adapter-management overhead.

paper_core_claims.claim: Low-magnitude task-vector entries can dilute influential updates and sign disagreement can cancel updates when models are merged.

TIES trims each task vector to its top-k magnitude entries, elects each coordinate's sign by total signed movement, averages only nonzero entries aligned to that sign, scales the result and adds it to the common initialization.
Across T5, IA3 and ViT settings TIES usually improves over the strongest tested merging baseline, with both tuned and fixed k=20%, lambda=1 recipes.

paper_core_claims.claim: Classical refinement verification conditions are unsound for lazy evaluation because they may assume refinements of free variables bound to divergent expressions.
Div, Wnf and Fin strata distinguish computations that may diverge, reduce to a value, or reduce to a finite value, so only sound environmental refinements enter SMT conditions.
The algorithmic lambda-D system restricts predicates to QF-EUFLIAD, uses stratified fixpoint constants, and soundly approximates evaluation-based implication with decidable SMT validity.
The proven guarantee is type preservation and crash-freedom; unlabelled refinement types retain partial correctness and do not require termination.

representation_or_carrier: The main carriers are refinement types, dependent function contracts, Div/Wnf/Fin labels, environments, measures, qualifiers, decreasing metrics, verification conditions and typed Core-like expressions. paper_core_claims.claim: Refinement reflection strengthens a total function's output type with an equality to its definition, so dependent application exposes precise instances without universal axioms.
Propositions-as-types plus dependent functions, pairs and sums can encode natural-deduction proofs while SMT handles quantifier-free obligations.
PLE repeatedly unfolds enabled guarded definitions and is sound, complete for the paper's equational-proof relation, and terminating under total reflected definitions and transparent environments.
In the reported suite PLE reduces proof code from 1,524 to 638 lines while total verification time changes from 148.76 to 150.88 seconds and SMT queries rise from 1,626 to 4,068.
The approach verifies selected arithmetic, typeclass-law, higher-order, SAT/unification and deterministic-parallelism properties in LiquidHaskell.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A total Haskell function is an executable definition and a logical carrier: reflection compiles its guarded definition into the output refinement, while proof functions inhabit specifications. PLE evaluates reflected applications in the solver logic to validate equational properties.
representation_or_carrier: Carriers include refinement types, proof-returning Haskell functions, reflected function symbols, guarded definitions, lambda-R programs, lambda-S QF-EUFLIA terms, definitional and logical environments, unfold instances and benchmark modules. specification_language: Dependent refinements encode pre/postconditions and arbitrary natural-deduction proposition structure using functions, pairs and sums; native predicates stay quantifier-free. Reflected equalities expose total user functions. This is expressive for pure functional properties but requires user specifications, termination metrics, case/induction structure and helper lemma instantiations; effects, resources, privacy, deployment and lifecycle are not specified.
compiler_or_generator: LiquidHaskell checks totality, converts reflected definitions to guarded form, defunctionalizes higher-order terms into first-order SMT symbols, generates QF-EUFLIA VCs and lets PLE unfold enabled instances until proof or fixpoint. The compiler does not synthesize induction or arbitrary lemmas, and historical class-method/module/data-type engineering restrictions narrow the accepted source language.
interpreter_or_runtime: Proofs and refinements are compile-time artifacts; proof arguments are intended never to be evaluated and can be rewritten to unit. Executable code uses ordinary lazy Haskell runtime. PLE is a verifier-side interpreter of logical definitions, not runtime monitoring. The trusted path includes LiquidHaskell translation, SMT answers and assumed combinators, and the paper notes mature proof assistants instead emit small checkable certificates.
composition_rule: Dependent function application instantiates reflected definitions; proof combinators and natural-deduction constructors compose propositions; recursion supplies induction; PLE composes guarded unfoldings and SMT theory reasoning; verified typeclass-style laws constrain parallel reducers. This is symbolic proof composition, not a cross-representation composer or adaptive router.
state_or_effect_model: The core theory is pure, total functional evaluation. Divergence is tracked as a soundness boundary and non-total functions cannot be reflected. Mutable state, exceptions, I/O, nondeterminism, probability, distributed failures and lifecycle effects are outside the core proof system.
uncertainty_model: Soundness and completeness judgments are categorical relative to the formal systems and assumptions. Completeness means: if a proof exists in the paper's equational-proof relation, PLE finds it; it does not mean all true functional properties are automatically proved. Evaluation reports one machine and aggregate counts without repeated-run uncertainty. Failure may mean a false goal, missing induction/lemma, nontransparent environment, implementation restriction, timeout or specification/tool defect; no calibrated confidence is supplied.

paper_core_claims.claim: Evidence translation can be encoded as an Eff computation that receives a typed runtime context of handler evidence, letting a call site select the applicable handler directly.
Tail-resumptive operations can execute under the selected handler context without yielding, whereas general operations use multi-prompt control and guarded resumptions.
The Haskell interface expresses Reader, exceptions, state, nondeterminism and parsing with effect signatures separated from handlers.

Reported performance is workload dependent: EV is 49 ms versus 9 ms for Pure/MTL in Counter, 83 ms versus 247-327 ms for Pure/MTL in Counter5, and scales constantly with added Reader layers in the tested layered arrangement.
The library is an implementation-oriented realization of the evidence-translation semantics rather than a new proof of the underlying type-safety theorem.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is an effect-indexed Haskell computation Eff e a whose ordinary value result is accompanied by a statically constrained effect context. Operations are first-class records selected through type-class evidence and interpreted by handlers; a handler transforms an extended effect context into a smaller one.
representation_or_carrier: The carriers are Haskell GADTs/newtypes, heterogeneous type-level effect lists, runtime Context lists of marker-handler-transform triples, Op records, Ctl pure/yield nodes, continuation/resumption functions and Local IORefs. The type-level effect list is intended to mirror the order of runtime handler evidence.
specification_language: Effect signatures are ordinary parameterized Haskell records whose Op fields state argument, result, residual-effect and answer types; :? membership constraints declare which effects a computation may use. This specifies effect availability and handler order but not semantic pre/postconditions, quantitative resource limits, probabilistic calibration, privacy policy or lifecycle obligations. Identical duplicate effect types collapse under the type-class encoding unless wrapped in distinct newtypes.
compiler_or_generator: GHC type checking and specialization compile effect-indexed source. Type-class subContext selection produces a typed runtime suffix, evidence translation passes that context to calls, tail-resumptive function/value operations can inline into direct calls, and non-tail operations compile to multi-prompt yields. No standalone source-to-source compiler, optimizer proof, automatic handler synthesis or artifact generator is supplied.
interpreter_or_runtime: runEff executes the Ctl substrate over the evidence context. Handlers add prompt markers and handler records; perform chooses the subcontext and operation; function runs directly under evidence while operation yields a continuation to a prompt. Unhandled operations and cross-context resumptions fail with runtime error. IORef-backed local state is saved and restored across resumptions using unsafe IO primitives.
composition_rule: Handlers compose by ordered context extension and masking; membership constraints select a matching effect subcontext; a handler eliminates the leading effect while preserving the residual computation; general operations may invoke resumptions zero, one or multiple times. The composition law is order-sensitive, identical-effect ambiguity needs nominal wrappers, arbitrary handler masking is not exposed, and scoped resumption is checked dynamically rather than proven by the Haskell type system.
state_or_effect_model: The library directly models Reader, exceptions, mutable/local state, nondeterminism and parser control as algebraic-style signatures plus handlers. Tail-resumptive operations and general operations have distinct runtime paths. Local state relies on IORefs with resumption restoration. Real I/O, concurrency, cancellation, transactions, distributed failure and resource lifetime are not given a complete semantic treatment.
uncertainty_model: Typing and operational claims are categorical relative to the evidence-translation assumptions and trusted marker primitive. Benchmarks report Criterion timing values from one GHC 8.6.5/x86-64 workstation configuration without confidence intervals, raw samples, variance, allocation profiles or cross-platform replication. Performance is highly benchmark-specific, and runtime errors, type-class ambiguity, unsafe marker uniqueness and implementation defects are not represented as calibrated uncertainty.

paper_core_claims.claim: Separating abstract operation signatures from handlers permits programs to be written independently of concrete effect interpretations and permits handlers to interpret subsets while forwarding the rest.
Deep handlers wrap the continuation with the same handler; shallow handlers expose an unhandled continuation and can better express some producer/consumer pipelines.
The lambda-eff calculus has deterministic small-step semantics, termination for well-typed terms, and type soundness for closed empty-effect computations.
Effect handlers can be encoded in Haskell using free or continuation monads, type families/classes and quasiquotes, and can also be implemented with delimited continuations in OCaml, SML and Racket.

The reported continuation-handler implementation is commonly about two-thirds of baseline performance, but results vary: it wins over unrevised flat pipes, loses to revised and nested pipes, and is nearly identical on the AOP case.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function is a computation whose type carries an effect signature. Its abstract operations specify callable interfaces, while handlers supply return and operation clauses that transform a computation with input effects into a result computation with output effects. Continuations expose the remaining computation to each clause.
representation_or_carrier: The formal carriers are lambda-eff values, thunked computations, finite operation signatures, handlers, continuation-passing operation applications and call-by-push-value computation types. Implementations use Haskell Comp/operation GADTs/type classes/type families/quasiquoted syntax, free/codensity/continuation monads, or dynamic handler stacks plus delimited continuations in ML/Racket.
specification_language: Operation declarations specify universal/existential type parameters, arguments and return types; computation types specify allowed effects; handler types specify handled and residual effects plus result type. This is a structured effect contract, not a general semantic pre/postcondition language. The Haskell encoding uses Handles constraints and functional dependencies rather than native effect rows, so parent-handler order can leak into types and handlers are not first-class.
compiler_or_generator: Template Haskell parsers and quasiquoters generate operation wrappers, handler types, Handles instances, forwarding boilerplate and convenient wrappers. GHC compiles the continuation/free encodings and may optimize abstraction. The other language sketches use dynamic handler stacks and shift0/reset0. The work does not prove that generated Haskell is a semantics-preserving compilation of lambda-eff or provide a reproducible compiler package.
interpreter_or_runtime: Closed and open handlers interpret return/operation nodes; open handlers forward unmatched operations. Deep handlers reinstall themselves around continuations, while shallow handlers leave continuations unhandled. The Haskell continuation encoding dispatches clauses through type classes; the ML/Racket sketch keeps handlers in a dynamic stack and captures delimited continuations. An operation that escapes all handlers raises an exception in the dynamic implementation.
composition_rule: Handler composition is ordinary function composition over computations, with an ordered nesting that determines which clause handles an operation. Open handlers forward residual operations, return clauses transform final values, and operation clauses may discard or invoke continuations once or many times. Composition is modular but not generally commutative: order, deep versus shallow continuation wrapping, handler parameters and duplicate operations affect behavior and sometimes types.
state_or_effect_model: The paper models state, logging, I/O, exceptions/failure, nondeterministic and random choice, parsing, streaming/pipes and AOP-style interception. Effects are free-theory operations with no equations; their meanings come from handlers. The calculus is terminating and excludes unrestricted recursion, whereas Haskell examples use recursion, IO, laziness and undefined, so formal guarantees do not transfer automatically to the full implementation.
uncertainty_model: Formal results are categorical within the simply typed terminating lambda-eff calculus and are supported by proof sketches, not mechanization. Criterion samples each benchmark ten times, yet the paper presents single millisecond values without dispersion or confidence intervals. The AOP generator fixes seed 42 in the repository, but other run environment details and raw samples are absent. Performance depends strongly on encoding, rewrite rules, workload and nesting.

Effect composition does not itself provide semantic pre/postconditions, calibrated probability, distributed-effect protocols or registry lifecycle governance.

paper_core_claims.claim: A stochastic probability interface consisting of a positive unbiased density estimator and its corresponding unbiased density sampler permits density estimates to appear safely in numerators and denominators of Monte Carlo ratios.
Lambda-SP combines discrete/continuous sampling, conditioning, higher-order functions, stochastic control flow, programmable inference, first-class marginalization and approximate normalization.
The type-directed translation compiles closed well-supported lambda-SP programs into unbiased density estimators and corresponding samplers.
Importance sampling, selected SMC steps and pseudomarginal MH remain sound with SPI estimates when absolute-continuity and properly-weighted hypotheses hold.

Across six case-study families, generated estimators are commonly 1-5x slower than hand-coded estimators but can be orders of magnitude faster than exact density evaluation; stochastic noise causes bounded but nonzero convergence degradation in the reported experiments.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A function may denote a deterministic map, a distribution, a normalized traced probabilistic program, an unnormalized measure program, or an inference algorithm. Its stochastic meaning is a measure paired with return-value semantics, while its compiled operational interface supplies randomized density estimates and, when normalized, samples carrying reciprocal-density information.
representation_or_carrier: Carriers include ground measurable spaces with reference measures, quasi-Borel spaces for higher-order functions, finite heterogeneous named traces, probability/subprobability/measure monads, P/M/D program types, inference combinators, stochastic density kernels, weighted samples and Julia Gen ChoiceMaps/Distribution traces. The density semantics and measure semantics are distinct but related by a type-indexed logical relation.
specification_language: Lambda-SP types distinguish distributions D, normalized traced programs P, unnormalized programs M, algorithms Alg/SMC/MCMC and deterministic higher-order functions. Named sample/observe, marginal and normalize constructs specify generative and inferential structure; the SPI specifies positivity, unbiasedness and corresponding sampling. Users must still supply primitive SPI implementations, custom proposals and support conditions; general nonprobabilistic pre/postconditions, resources, privacy and lifecycle are outside the language.
compiler_or_generator: The d{·} translation maps each source type and term to randomized target-language code implementing the SPI. It composes independent estimates for sequencing, builds reverse/conditional inference machinery, compiles marginalization through importance sampling and compiles normalization through the chosen inference algorithm. Correctness is relative to primitives satisfying their SPI and all proposal/target absolute-continuity obligations; the compiler does not prove these obligations automatically.
interpreter_or_runtime: GenSP extends Gen.jl with SPDistribution, random_weighted and estimate_logpdf, representing inference algorithms themselves as stochastic distributions over ChoiceMaps. The runtime uses weighted proposals, importance sampling, SMC, MCMC, marginal distributions and nested inference. Random traces and weights are operational artifacts; exact posterior inference is generally not performed, and normalization denotes the finite inference algorithm's approximate output distribution rather than the exact posterior.
composition_rule: Probabilistic programs compose monadically over disjoint named traces; density estimates multiply when conditionally independent; marginal and normalize accept user-selected inference algorithms; SMC steps and MCMC kernels compose with constructed conditional/time-reversal counterparts. Composition preserves unbiasedness only under positivity, independence, absolute-continuity/support and algorithm-specific proper-weighting conditions. Approximation at nested marginal/normalize sites introduces cumulative runtime-variance tradeoffs.
state_or_effect_model: Random sampling, observation/conditioning, trace allocation, failure/subprobability mass and approximate inference are explicit effects. Named traces expose stochastic control flow and choices. The model covers discrete and continuous probability with higher-order functions but assumes finite traces, unique names on composed traces and absolute continuity relative to selected reference measures; concurrency, distributed state, resource lifetime and external side effects are not formalized.
uncertainty_model: The semantic uncertainty is measure-theoretic: probability measures, unnormalized measures, densities relative to reference measures, unbiased positive random estimators, sampler/reciprocal pairs, importance weights and convergence in the infinite-computation limit. Estimator variance affects finite MCMC acceptance and SMC weights but is not statically bounded. Empirically, ten 300-iteration MCMC runs give about ±3% acceptance-rate margins; several 'exact' convergence baselines are actually very-high-particle approximations, and the paper does not provide a general calibrated finite-time error certificate.

paper_core_claims.claim: The idealized probabilistic metalanguage has denotational semantics for score-result probability measures and measurable configuration-based operational semantics for continuous sampling.

Within the recursion-free language and a perfect normalization assumption, deterministic evaluation is total, probabilistic evaluation is stochastic, and denotational semantics is sound and adequate for operational evaluation.

paper_core_claims.claim: A countable-product-preserving functor category supplies function spaces unavailable in ordinary measurable spaces, lifts probability monads and conservatively extends first-order semantics.
The semantics validates a corrected normalize-resample program equation used by sequential Monte Carlo and an importance-sampling equation for continuous densities.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A deterministic function is a measurable map at first order and a natural transformation in the higher-order functor model. A probabilistic function is a Kleisli arrow whose result is a probability measure over nonnegative score-result pairs. Higher-order probabilistic programs are suspended by T(A), and distributions over functions are represented indirectly by probability distributions over measurable codes rather than a measurable function space.
representation_or_carrier: First-order carriers are measurable spaces, probability spaces P(A), products and countable sums. Operational carriers are measurable spaces of closures/configurations with stochastic transition relations and accumulated scores. Higher-order carriers are countable-product-preserving functors Meas-op to Set, with Yoneda embeddings and lifted Giry/score monads. Continuous likelihoods use normalized continuous density functions over separable metrizable spaces with selected sigma-finite base measures.
specification_language: The metalanguage separates deterministic and probabilistic typing judgments and provides return/let, products, countable sums, measurable constants, sample, score and norm; the higher-order extension adds functions, thunks and force, and density types specify continuous likelihoods. It deliberately includes constants for every measurable function and infinitary forms, so it is a mathematical compiler target rather than an implementable user language. It specifies probabilistic effects and evidence errors but not general pre/postconditions, resources, security, concurrency or lifecycle policies.
compiler_or_generator: No compiler or code generator is implemented. The authors position the calculus as a semantic target for practical languages and use denotational equality to justify compiler optimizations, a normalize-resample SMC transformation and importance sampling. These are equation-level correctness results under semantic assumptions, not a verified compilation pipeline or a proof of an entire inference implementation.
interpreter_or_runtime: The paper defines a formal small-step runtime over measurable closures: deterministic reductions are functions, probabilistic reductions are stochastic relations, score multiplies accumulated weight, sample branches by a distribution and norm invokes an abstract perfect normalizer. There is no executable interpreter, sampler, numerical backend or empirical runtime. Exact norm is semantic; it must not be read as an available finite Monte Carlo procedure.
composition_rule: Return/let compose through the commutative monad P(R>=0 x -), multiplying scores and integrating over intermediate results. Stochastic relations compose by integration. At higher order, lifted monads, Cartesian closure, lambda/application and thunk/force compose functions and probabilistic computations. The SMC equation inserts normalization, evidence scoring and resampling at a top-level score, reverting to the original term for infinite evidence in v3. General normalization is not a monad morphism, because Fubini fails for all measures.

paper_core_claims.claim: Stochastic lambda calculus augments universal functional computation with random choice, and Church packages this foundation into a compositional probabilistic programming language with recursion, symbols, memoization and inference queries.

Every computable distribution is representable by a stochastic lambda expression, motivating the broader universality thesis that any reasonable computable probabilistic model can be represented in the calculus.

paper_core_claims.claim: Conditional inference can be expressed inside Church by recursive rejection sampling, while practical PPLs may substitute MCMC, SMC, enumeration, HMC, variational or programmable inference.
The formal PLoT hypothesis identifies reusable concepts with stochastic functions in a universal PPL, combining probabilistic gradedness with symbolic compositionality and open-ended productivity.

A compact Church tug-of-war/ping-pong concept library predicts condition-level human strength judgments in two 2012 experiments with reported aggregate correlations r=.98 and r=.97 and median participant correlations r=.92 and r=.86.
Probabilistic execution traces and nested queries provide reusable representations for mental simulation, counterfactual reasoning, planning, inverse planning and program-based concept learning.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A concept is a reusable stochastic function: its proximal meaning is its program definition, its compositional role comes from calls among functions and symbols, and its inferential meaning emerges from conditional queries over the joint generative program. representation_or_carrier: The formal carrier is a call-by-value stochastic lambda term with variables, abstraction, application and uniform choice; a term induces a distribution or subprobability over terminal values. Church adds Scheme values, ERPs, recursion, symbols, higher-order functions and stochastic memo tables. Cognitive models are libraries of concept functions plus observations and queries; runtime carriers include sampled worlds, latent variables, program execution traces, MCMC samples and nested inferred programs.
specification_language: Church specifies generative knowledge through composable stochastic function definitions and separates reusable concept libraries from query and condition expressions. Symbols permit open-ended entities, mem fixes random properties per argument, ERPs specify priors, and recursive/nested query encodes conditioning, planning and meta-inference. The language does not specify general pre/postconditions, resource bounds, convergence requirements, neural realizations, governance, privacy or lifecycle policy, and many examples rely on informal helper functions or simulator primitives.

paper_core_claims.claim: Naming Knightian nondeterministic choices and tracking their renaming/disjointness with grades yields a commutative, affine and distributive account that supports dataflow-style categorical and monoidal composition.
ImP is a FinStochSurj-graded distributive Markov category, equivalently a graded Kleisli model based on finite stochastic maps, and it combines finite probability with Knightian nondeterminism.
Mapping an ImP morphism to the convex image of its stochastic map defines an identity-on-objects op-lax functor to the convex-powerset Kleisli category, with R(g o f) contained in R(g) o R(f).
Preserving shared named Knightian choices can make the inclusion strict, producing a tighter finitely generated convex uncertainty region than composition after forgetting the names.
Under a precise FinStochSurj-graded distributive Markov functor and a factorization of the convex-image interpretation, any such functor from ImP is faithful.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A program denotes a morphism in a graded distributive Markov category. Ordinary values are finite objects, Bernoulli sampling is a grade-I stochastic morphism, and each one-use Knightian choice is a named graded morphism. Sequencing, tensor/dataflow juxtaposition, copying, discarding and finite case analysis compose these morphisms while grades record the sample space and permissible regradings of uncertain choices.
representation_or_carrier: The concrete carrier is finite: objects are finite sets; precise probabilistic computations are stochastic matrices; a grade gamma is a finite set/sample space connected by surjective stochastic maps; and an ImP morphism X to Y at grade gamma is a stochastic map gamma x X to Y. Closed computations induce finitely generated convex subsets of finite probability simplices. Open terms retain intensional named-choice structure that is intentionally not quotiented to convex sets.
specification_language: The paper gives a typed first-order functional metalanguage with immutable sequencing, finite sums/products, if-then-else, fair bernoulli, named knight(a) choices and explicit grade coercions c_f. Grades specify which uncertain names/sample spaces a term uses, while equations specify associativity, commutativity, weakening, hoisting and graded algebraic laws. It does not specify recursion, higher-order functions, conditioning, observations, mutable state, operational resource budgets, numerical tolerances, deployment contracts or lifecycle policy; even practical coercion inference is future work.
compiler_or_generator: No compiler, elaborator or code generator is implemented or validated. The syntax-to-category interpretation is a denotational construction, and the paper explicitly leaves practical grade/coercion inference to future work. The Kan-extension result extracts the convex-powerset functor mathematically but is not a compiler and supplies no algorithmic complexity or executable translation receipt.
interpreter_or_runtime: No interpreter or inference runtime is supplied. Matrix calculations and program equations illustrate denotations in the finite model, but there is no parser, evaluator, sampler, conditioning engine, robust-statistics procedure, benchmark or artifact. Statistical inference for a probabilistic programming language with imprecise probability is listed as an open practical question.
composition_rule: For f in ImP_gamma(X,Y) and g in ImP_epsilon(Y,Z), graded composition uses the tensor grade gamma x epsilon, swaps/reassociates the grade factors and composes the corresponding stochastic maps; tensor juxtaposition composes independent dataflow branches. Surjective stochastic regradings express renaming, forgetting or coupling of Knightian sources. The convex-set projection is only op-lax: R(g o f) is a subset of R(g) o R(f), because the former preserves one shared epsilon-choice across intermediate outcomes while the latter may choose separately for each outcome.
state_or_effect_model: The only modeled effects are finite probability and named one-use Knightian nondeterminism. Commutativity, affinity and distributive finite case analysis are deliberate laws; the model excludes mutable memory, recursion, unbounded iteration and repeated learning about an urn. Choice names encode intensional sharing/dependence and grades encode reindexing, but there is no operational heap, concurrency, external I/O, persistent trace, failure recovery or deployment state.
uncertainty_model: Precise uncertainty is a finite probability vector or stochastic matrix. Imprecision is the convex image obtained by ranging over probability distributions on a finite grade/sample space; only finitely generated convex sets over finite outcomes occur. Named Knightian choices distinguish shared from independent unknown probabilities and thereby retain dependence information lost by the ordinary convex-powerset monad. This is not Bayesian updating: there are no observations, posterior conditioning, interval estimators, calibration guarantees, convergence rates or complexity bounds, and iteration/infinite spaces remain open.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The language is deliberately minimal and first-order: it has no first-class functions, recursion, mutation or unbounded iteration.

Outcomes, grades and stochastic matrices are finite, and the resulting convex uncertainty sets are finitely generated; infinite domains, metrics, domain theory and unbounded Knightian choices are future work.
Each Knightian urn is fresh and used once. The model does not learn an unknown ratio through repeated observations or frequencies.
The semantics represents imprecise prior choice but provides no conditioning, Bayesian update, likelihood, posterior inference or decision rule.
The paper explicitly leaves statistical inference for an imprecise-probability programming language as an open practical question.
No compiler, interpreter, code repository, executable artifact, benchmark or empirical evaluation is supplied.
Practical grade/coercion inference is future work, so the formal notation is not yet an ergonomic implementable type-and-effect system.
The correspondence between graded distributive Markov categories and graded commutative affine relative monads is conjectured to be a biequivalence but is not proved.
Theorem 5.6 establishes an op-lax inclusion, not equality; tighter bounds arise because named dependence is retained, not because all uncertainty has been eliminated or calibrated.

Theorem 6.2 is a conditional faithfulness result under a specific FinStochSurj grading, strict preservation of structure and factorization through convex images; it is not universal maximality over all formalisms.

Open-term intensional names cannot simply be quotiented away while retaining both desiderata: the forall-exists quotient loses commutativity and the exists-forall quotient loses if-hoisting/coproducts.
The authors leave open how results depend on the particular grading subcategory, so alternative grade systems may change the theory.
The convex-powerset model discussed in comparison is noncommutative in the relevant sense; translating to it forgets shared-choice dependencies and may enlarge bounds.
The work proves semantic properties, not computational complexity, numerical stability, sampling convergence, calibration or scalability.
No result connects this finite categorical model to neural weights, learned Function OS assets, ignition epsilon, frozen Psi_0 or production governance.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not implement or empirically validate an imprecise-probability programming system.
It does not provide posterior updating, inference algorithms, convergence guarantees, error bars or complexity bounds.
It does not show that arbitrary continuous, higher-order, recursive or infinite-state probabilistic programs fit the finite ImP construction.
It does not prove unconditional maximality across all imprecise-probability theories; its theorem has explicit categorical and factorization hypotheses.
It does not establish that convex-set equality is a fully compositional equivalence for open programs.
It does not supply empirical validation of ignition, a probability law for ignition epsilon, neural-function equivalence or artifact lifecycle closure.
